teams.heading: Sam Underhill ruled out of November Tests after being stood down
teams.body: England flanker Sam Underhill has been stood down with immediate effect following an injury update from Bath, ruling him out of the upcoming Nations Championship fixtures. His absence for the November Tests, including the meeting with Australia, forces Steve Borthwick into a significant back-row reshuffle. Underhill’s unavailability comes as a major blow to the national side's defensive stability. Exeter’s Greg Fisilau and Bath teammate Guy Pepper are among the leading candidates to fill the void as Borthwick considers his revised selection options.

teams.heading: Darcy Graham ruled out for remainder of year with bicep injury
teams.body: Scotland and Edinburgh winger Darcy Graham will remain sidelined for the rest of the 2026 calendar year following his ruptured bicep injury. The setback, which was described by Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt as a "freakish" occurrence, ensures the winger will miss the upcoming November international programme. With his recovery timeline extending until after Christmas, the focus remains on his rehabilitation programme as the national side prepares for the Nations Championship and the subsequent fixtures against New Zealand.

teams.heading: Josh Adams aims for full fitness before Wales face Japan next
teams.body: Josh Adams is nearing a return to action as he targets a place in the Wales squad for the upcoming autumn internationals. While he continues to manage his recovery, Adams stated, “It’s important that you navigate your way through correctly and there’s no rush,” with a club return for Cardiff expected before the November Tests.

teams.heading: Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa signs two-year deal with Super Rugby champions Hurricanes
teams.body: Former Moana Pasifika back-rower Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa has committed his future to the Hurricanes, signing a two-year contract with the reigning Super Rugby Pacific champions. The 22-year-old earned his maiden All Blacks call-up during this year's Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series, featuring in mid-week matches against the Sharks and the Lions. Hurricanes head coach Clark Laidlaw praised the forward’s “destructive power,” stating: “He’s someone who has already played Super Rugby at such a high level and played so well at such a young age.”

teams.body: Siya Kolisi has won significant praise from his new Stormers team-mates after travelling from Perth to Galway to join the squad while sidelined from international duty. Forwards coach Rito Hlungwani highlighted the double World Cup-winning captain’s “humble” nature, noting that his decision to join the touring party immediately after missing the Wallabies Test was aimed at bonding with the squad. Number eight Hacjivah Dayimani added that the gesture was highly appreciated, confirming the superstar’s commitment to his return to Cape Town rugby.
